newsitem.title: USA: Sun Micro completes JavaBeans specification.
newsitem.headline: Sun Micro completes JavaBeans specification.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc released its completed specification for JavaBeans, the architecture designed to enable developers to use components running across a variety of computing platforms using Java.

Jon Kannegaard, vice president of software products at Sun's JavaSoft subsidiary, said the Javabeans applications programming interface (API) specification is being released two months ahead of schedule.
He said plans to increase the number of employees at the JavaSoft unit to 500 by the end of its June 1997 fiscal year is aimed at spreading the use of Java technology.

Kannegaard said in an interview that the increase in the fast-growing unit's staffing plans from its previous estimate of 300 to 350 positions by the end of the fiscal year would not involve any change in the business plan for JavaSoft.

"The focus for this year is to get the platform in place," he said of Java, which is a set of computing technologies developed by Sun that enables developers to develop software that can run on otherwise incompatible systems.
"What it means is we're going to do more, sooner, better, faster," he said of the decision to expand JavaSoft more rapidly. "We want to get the market going for JavaBeans."
By using the JavaBeans specification, developers can build and take advantage of re-usable software components that are designed to run across major computer platforms.

JavaSoft said the architecture enables developers to run applications in Microsoft Corp's COM standard, the OpenDoc standard promoted by Apple Computer Inc and International Business Machines Corp, and Netscape Communications Corp's LiveConnect platform.
But Microsoft, which has been promoting its own ActiveX Compontent Object Model implementation to provide similar capabilities, was not among those endorsing JavaBeans.
Analysts believe that Microsoft, as a licensee of the Java API set, will be required to implement JavaBeans eventually, but will continue to promote ActiveX aggressively.

"We agree with Microsoft on a lot, but where we part company is we fundamentally believe that there are and will be interesting platforms aside from (Microsoft's Windows) Win32," said Kannegaard, adding JavaSoft is committed to its platform- independent, or platform-neutral, strategy.
The JavaBeans specification will be included in the next release of Java, due out in early calendar 1997, and will be distributed in a preliminary development kit in December.

The completed JavaBeans specification incorporated contributions from a variety of companies, including Borland International, IBM and its Lotus Development Corp unit, Netscape, Novell Inc, Oracle Corp, Silicon Graphics Inc, and Symantec.
"By using Java Beans technology they're (developers are) shielded from the component platform wars," Kannegaard said.

Sun is planning a developer gathering in Long Beach, Calif., on November 6 to provide further details on JavaBeans, and it said further information about the specification is available on the Internet at (http://java.sun.com/beans).
